steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how has the implant been since we last saw you? I usually hear one of three things. Rock solid, something feels a little off, or something is bothering you. Which one is closest?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Rock Solid
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's what a well-placed implant should feel like, so natural you forget which tooth it is. It means the work you invested in is paying off.

(Let them enjoy it. Then ask permission for the questions.)

steps.title: Something Feels a Little Off
steps.content:
I'm glad you mentioned that, {{contact_first_name}}. The gum around an implant needs its own attention, and small changes can start without you noticing. It's not anything you did wrong, and it's the reason we check in. When these things are caught early, they're usually simple to take care of. What got in the way of coming in, life getting busy or feeling like the implant didn't need checkups?

(Let them answer. Do not try to book yet.)

steps.title: Something Is Bothering Them
steps.content:
I'm glad you told me, {{contact_first_name}}. It's not anything you did wrong. The gum and bone around an implant are living tissue. Things can start there without you noticing. The sooner we look, the simpler it usually is to take care of. What got in the way of coming in, life getting busy or feeling like the implant didn't need checkups?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not try to book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, can I ask you a few quick questions about anything else you've noticed?

(Wait for the yes. Most people stop thinking about an implant once it feels solid. The questions find what they'd never think to mention.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to what you noticed in a moment. First, can I ask you a few quick questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment.)

First, around the implant. Any tenderness, swelling, or bleeding when you brush or floss near it?

Do you ever notice food catching around it, or floss snagging nearby?

How does your bite feel on it, chewing on that side like normal?

How about the rest of your teeth, any sensitivity or gum bleeding?

When was your last professional cleaning, here or anywhere?

How do you feel about your smile these days, still smiling in photos?

Finally, any changes in your health or medications since we last saw you?

(Recap what you wrote down, including what they mentioned at the start, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, between what you mentioned first and anything else, which one would you most like to take care of?

(If what they mentioned at the start is the only thing on the list, that's the answer. Tap the button and continue.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment.)

First, around the implant. Any tenderness, swelling, or bleeding when you brush or floss near it?

Do you ever notice food catching around it, or floss snagging nearby?

How does your bite feel on it, chewing on that side like normal?

How about the rest of your teeth, any sensitivity or gum bleeding?

When was your last professional cleaning, here or anywhere?

How do you feel about your smile these days, still smiling in photos?

Finally, any changes in your health or medications since we last saw you?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one would you most like to take care of?

(Tap their answer below. If nothing came up, that's still a good call. Use the second button.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each and let them answer.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a week or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer. If it fits, you can say "Got it.")

Is it something you experience like 1 to 2 times a month, or is it more often than that?

(Let them answer. If it fits, you can say "I see." or "I understand.")

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with meals, talking with people, or smiling in photos?

(Let them answer. If they name an impact, reflect only what they said about meals, talking, or photos. If not, you can say "Got it, thank you.")

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Read back their three answers: how long, how often, what it gets in the way of.)

So it's been bothering you a while, and it comes up more than once in a while. At its worst it gets in the way of what you mentioned. Did I get that right?

(Say what they named: meals, talking with people, or smiling in photos. Let them answer. If they correct you, take the correction and move on.)

And it sounds like you'd really like to eat, talk, and smile without thinking about it. Is that fair to say?

(Most people say yes. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. A quick implant health check does one thing. {{provider_name}} looks at the implant and the gum and bone holding it. That catches anything small before it becomes something big. If everything is as solid as it feels, we'll tell you that too. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for that quick implant health check, so we can take a look at {{main_concern}}. Does that sound reasonable?

(Say "does that sound reasonable", not "does that sound good". Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. No pressure. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Uncover the Real Concern
steps.content:
Okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm not going to push you on it. What's the part giving you pause?

(Let them answer. Then tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Why Did They Stop?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad everything is feeling solid.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in?

(Let them answer. Listen all the way through. Do not argue with it.)

(Tap the button below that is closest to their reason.)

steps.title: If They Say: “I was happy with the results”
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}, and that's the best reason there is. When the implant feels like your own tooth, coming back stops feeling urgent. One thing worth knowing. The implant itself is built to last, but the gum and bone holding it are living tissue. The early warning signs there don't hurt, so you won't feel them until later. A quick check confirms it's as healthy as it feels.

Does that make sense?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for that quick check so it stays the way it is. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: Cost or Budget
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}, and I'm glad you told me. An implant check is a short visit, and it costs a fraction of what the implant did. And you're not committing to anything. It's one visit so we can make sure the gum and bone around it are healthy.

Does that seem fair?

(Let them answer.)

(Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for that quick check. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “Life got busy”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up fast, and an implant check slides down the list. It happens to everyone. The visit is quick, and we can find a time that works around your schedule.

Would that work?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in at a time that's easy for you. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “I’ll come back if it bothers me”
steps.content:
That's a fair way to think about it, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd share is that trouble around an implant starts quietly. The gum and bone can change for a long time before anything hurts. Caught early, it's usually a simple fix. Caught late, it can put the implant itself at risk.

Does that sound right?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so we catch anything early. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: They Moved or Tried Another Provider
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change. If you're still in the area, we'd love to see you again. Your x-rays and whole history are in your file, so we can pick up right where you left off.

Would that be okay?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “I thought implants were permanent”
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's a fair question, and you're half right.

Can I ask, has anything changed around it, like the gum feeling different or food catching?

(Let them answer. Do not give dental advice on the call.)

The implant itself is permanent. The gum and bone holding it are living tissue, and they need the same care your natural teeth do. Think of a good roof. It lasts for decades, but you still keep the gutters clear. Problems around an implant start small and cost little to catch early. Left alone, they cost a lot.

The check is how {{provider_name}} keeps the permanent part permanent.

Would it help to know it's solid, instead of assuming?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m embarrassed I haven’t been in”
steps.content:
Please don't be, {{contact_first_name}}. Nobody here is keeping score.

Can I ask, was it one thing that got in the way, or did it just drift off the list?

(Let them answer. Stay warm.)

Once an implant feels solid, it's natural to stop thinking about it. That's a sign the work was done well, not something you did wrong. The only thing embarrassment does is keep people away until a small thing becomes a big one.

{{provider_name}} would rather see you now than a year from now. We'd take a look at the implant and the gum around it and get your file current.

Would it feel better to just get that first step done?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m considering another option”
steps.content:
That's fair. Can I ask what you're looking at, like a general dentist, another office, or just leaving it?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other option.)

Those can all make sense, and some people do well combining them. The part that's hard to compare from home is whether the implant is still solid underneath. {{provider_name}} already has your file, the scans and what was placed, so you're not starting over here.

Come in, get a straight answer on where things stand, and then compare. If the other option turns out to be the better fit, you'll be choosing it for a reason.

Is that a fair way to decide?

steps.title: Objection: Cost
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it the cost of the check itself, or the worry that it’ll turn into a big bill?

(Let them answer. Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

This first check is one appointment, not a treatment. You'll hear what anything past that costs before you decide on it. And since you've been here before, we're not starting from scratch, and starting from scratch is the expensive part.

The other side of it is what waiting is already costing you, the things you mentioned a minute ago. That's the part I'd hate to see keep adding up.

Can we at least get the look on the calendar?

steps.title: Objection: “I don’t have time”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it finding time for the first check, or the worry about a run of appointments like before?

(Let them answer.)

Right now we're only talking about one check. {{provider_name}} looks at the implant and tells you what it would take from there. Most of the time that’s nothing more than a clean bill of health. If something’s starting, you’ll hear that up front so you can decide. Nobody is signing you up for anything on the phone.

We'll fit that first check around your schedule, not the other way around.

Could you find a short window for that?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to talk to my spouse”
steps.content:
Of course. Is it more about the money side, or do you two just make these decisions together?

(Let them answer. If it's money, use the cost answer.)

That's fair, and I'm not asking you to commit to anything they'd need to weigh in on. Right now, all you can tell them is that the implant is due a look. After the check, you can tell them what's going on and what it would take. That's an easier conversation to have. And if they'd like to come along, they're welcome.

Can we pencil it in, and you can move it after you two talk?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Usually when someone says that, there's one specific thing on their mind. What's the part you'd want to think over?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

Okay. I'm not trying to rush you. The one thing I'd say is that the implant is due a look. It's been that way for a while, and it hasn't sorted itself out on its own. The check is how you get the information you'd be thinking with. You can think it over just as easily after you know what's going on.

Would it be easier to think it over once you have the answers?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I can do that, {{contact_first_name}}. What would you want it to cover, so I send the right thing?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

I'll be straight with you, though. Anything I send is going to be general. It can't tell you what's realistic for the implant specifically. That takes {{provider_name}} looking at the implant and the gum around it, and that's one short check.

Let's do both. I'll send the information, and we'll put a time on the calendar. If what I send answers your question, you can call and cancel, no problem.

Does doing both work for you?
